findings.sourceCause: Main previously had no requestSingleInstanceLock call; each same-profile launch registered runtime startup and could independently open SQLite/services.

contract: Resolve the selected profile to an absolute realpath (including Windows casing, namespaced path and junction aliases), then set userData before requesting the Electron native lock.
Lock rejection exits with code0 and never registers whenReady startup; no SQLite, feature services, tray or companion windows initialize in that process.
Real app second-instance events queue until the primary runtime and main window are initialized; a pending request coalesces, then restores a minimized main window, shows it and focuses it.
Different profile paths keep independent native singleton identities. Do not introduce an application-wide singleton or change the app name per profile.
Disposal ignores further activation but retains the native lock through database shutdown until process exit.
Canonicalization creates the profile directory if absent; it does not migrate, rewrite, delete or open saved files.
